propositions: Currently, scripts/check_config_reads.py proves config fields are consumed but cannot prove that ONLY approved composition roots and provider boundaries read ambient config and credentials, allowing silent unauthorized reads below the seam.

A new AST gate must detect six categories of prohibited config/credential access: ambient env read, helper-shim env read, load_config call, literal-getattr env equivalent, provider-credential read, and configurable adapter default/backend reload — each firing only outside approved seams.

The gate must reuse gen_env_registry's scan, KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS matchers, and _is_os_environ detection rather than duplicate AST parsing logic, and must resolve callee and receiver aliases to detect evasions like 'src = os.environ; src.get(SECRET)'.

Owner sets and credential boundaries must be derived at runtime from existing registries (_child_env.owned_secret_names, static @register decorator scan, gen_env_registry.scan) rather than hand-copied, with path-glob exceptions rejected structurally and unowned credential names triggering failures.

A legacy-exception set enumerates current below-seam reads so the gate is introducible without product-code changes, with C3 responsible for draining exceptions to empty and implementing credential sourcing semantics.

The gate must expose check(root)->list[str] and main(argv)->int contracts mirroring check_config_reads.py, pass all six-category synthetic fixtures and self-tests for bypass/unowned names/glob exceptions/missing rationale, run offline with no network dependency, and exit 0 on the current tree.
